name: Nicole Warren
bio:
Coach Nicole has been around volleyball nearly her entire life, starting club at just 8 years old and going on to play for more than 10 years. She played at Clackamas High School and also competed in beach volleyball around Oregon and California. Nicole earned a scholarship to continue her volleyball career at Blue Mountain Community College, but a back injury ultimately kept her from competing at the collegiate level.

Now in her 6th year of coaching and 3rd season with HVVC, Nicole has found a new way to share her love for the game. She especially enjoys teaching the mental and strategic sides of volleyball while helping shape confident, competitive athletes both on and off the court.

Outside of the gym, Nicole is probably still thinking about volleyball, or you can find her at a country concert, cheering on the Ducks, spending time on the lake in the summer, or hanging out with her dog and friends.

name: Mallory Cooper
bio:
Mallory played volleyball at West Linn High School and has continued her love for the sport primarily through beach volleyball. She has been coaching for several years, with 2026 marking her first season with HVVC. In the summer of 2026, she also created and hosted her own junior beach volleyball clinic on her home sand court, giving young athletes another opportunity to develop their skills and love for the game.

At just 20 years old, Mallory graduated with her bachelor’s degree in Psychology in June 2026 and is now continuing her education by pursuing a master’s degree in Mental Health Counseling. She enjoys bringing her background in psychology into her coaching and strives to create a positive, encouraging environment where athletes can build confidence both on and off the court.

name: Kanoelani Shadron
bio:
Kanoelani (or Kanoe) had an interest in volleyball before she even knew what sports were. Her next door neighbors would play in the front yard and her grandfather told her that one day she would play volleyball. She officially started playing club 12 years ago at the age of 12! Started as a middle and moved to full time setter. She has played for Clackamas High School, earning 3 varsity letters, Second Team All-American her junior year, and First Team All-American her senior year. As her grandfather predicted she went on to play volleyball to help support her dream of becoming a pediatric nurse at Briar Cliff University from 2021-2026.

From there Kanoe always knew she wanted to go on and share what she has learned to the new generations that are going to take the sport to new heights. She has been a coach at Siouxland Volleyball club in Iowa for the past three years and has helped the Boys Adrian C. Nelson High School Volleyball team. She is excited to finally coach for a club where she grew up and for her first season to be at HVVC.

name: Megan Reynolds
bio:
Coach Megan brings several years of club volleyball coaching experience, working with athletes from 12U through 16U. Prior to joining Happy Valley Volleyball Club, she coached with Mt. Hood Volleyball Club and Eastside FCA Volleyball Club, developing athletes across multiple age groups and competitive levels.

Her coaching philosophy focuses on strong fundamentals, discipline, confidence, teamwork, and game-focused training. Megan is passionate about developing the whole athlete and believes volleyball provides an incredible opportunity to teach accountability, resilience, leadership, communication, and what it means to be a great teammate.

Outside of volleyball, Megan is a Human Resources executive with nearly 20 years of leadership experience and a mom of two. She is excited to bring her experience and passion for youth athletics to Happy Valley Volleyball Club and looks forward to creating a competitive, positive environment where athletes are challenged, supported, and inspired to grow.

name: Charles Awounor
bio: Charles brings competitive experience and a development-focused approach to HVVC 16-2. His coaching style centers on building well-rounded athletes, technically sound, mentally tough, and hungry to compete. He is committed to creating a high-performance environment where every player is pushed to reach their full potential, both in the gym and in competition.

name: Kendal Ishida
bio:
Kendal brings a strong club volleyball background from her time with Athena VBC, where she developed a deep appreciation for the technical and mental sides of the game. She currently serves as an Assistant Varsity Coach at Clackamas High School and spends her summers continuing to grow as a coach at Guy Enriques Team Camp.

Kendal is passionate about helping young athletes build strong fundamentals, develop technical skills, and gain confidence both on and off the court. As a former setter, she especially enjoys teaching the details of the game, understanding the “why” behind each skill, and helping players develop their volleyball IQ. She strives to create a positive, supportive, and competitive environment where athletes can grow, challenge themselves, and build a genuine love for the game.

name: Christina Braks
bio:
Christina brings nine years of school and club playing experience and six seasons of coaching with Clackamas Junior and Sideout Volleyball, primarily working with seventh and eighth graders. She also continues to play recreationally.

Her hands-on coaching style emphasizes consistent feedback, strong foundational skills, and increasing volleyball IQ. Her favorite moments are watching athletes master skills they’ve worked hard on, from overhand serving to passing accuracy. She celebrates those accomplishments with the same pride she feels watching her own children succeed.

Christina is excited to bring her passion for volleyball and player development to HVVC!

Outside the gym, she stays busy keeping up with her four children in fifth, sixth, and eighth grades, her dog Ruby, and a cat Kiwi.

name: Sarah Borski
bio: Sarah Borski brings state championship, national club, and NCAA Division I playing experience to her leadership of Happy Valley Volleyball Club and HVVC Academy. Her approach combines a lifelong connection to volleyball with a commitment to helping young athletes grow as players, teammates, and people.

name: Harley Combs
bio:
Coach Harley is entering her fifth year of coaching volleyball and her first season with HVVC! A former multisport athlete through high school and college, she brings a competitive spirit and a passion for helping young athletes build confidence, develop their skills, and reach their full potential.

Outside of volleyball, she is the CFO of a commercial real estate company and enjoys running, staying active, and taking on new challenges. Most of all, she values time with her family and sharing her passion for sports with her daughter.

name: Kaia Iranon
bio:
Kaia is going into her second year coaching at HVVC and has been playing volleyball since the age of 11. She currently plays on Nelson High School’s varsity volleyball team, where she continues to grow as both a player and a leader. Volleyball has become a huge part of her life, and she is passionate about sharing the knowledge, experiences, and love for the game that she has developed throughout her playing career.

Kaia especially loves having the opportunity to teach, encourage, and inspire young girls in the volleyball world. She believes that volleyball is about more than just developing skills on the court; it is also about building confidence, learning to be a great teammate, developing a strong work ethic, and growing as a person. She strives to create a positive and competitive environment where athletes feel supported, challenged, and motivated to become the best versions of themselves.

One of Kaia’s favorite parts of coaching is watching athletes gain confidence, overcome challenges, and discover what they are capable of achieving. She loves being someone her players can look up to and hopes to inspire them to work hard, believe in themselves, and continue pursuing their goals both on and off the court. She is excited to continue growing as a coach and helping the next generation of volleyball players develop their skills, build lasting connections, and create a genuine love for the game.

name: Kendel Redding
bio:
Kendel brings a strong volleyball background from her time with ABC Apollos VBC and Mountainside High School Volleyball where she learned to be a leader, as well as a technically skilled defensive player. She has worked with children in sports for multiple years now, helping young ones build a foundation and curiosity for volleyball. This is her first year as a coach and is so excited!

Kendel cannot stress enough how important it is to help young athletes build strong fundamentals, learn how to be a good teammate, and build confidence. She knows how these skills in sports translate not only on the court, but to the rest of your life. As a former libero, she is extremely competitive, understands the game well, and knows how to sacrifice for a team. She hopes to leave athletes with a new found love for the game, a better player and a great time.

Outside of volleyball, Kendel works as a staff accountant at a public accounting firm where she is constantly learning, being pushed mentally, and managing balance. She has seen first-hand how her developed mental skills in sports has allowed herself to push for better jobs, opportunities and positions as she knows hard work and dedication pay off.

name: Kat Gierek
bio:
Kat brings a versatile background in coaching, player development, and club operations to HVVC. She is highly involved in our Academy programming, clinics, camps, and individual skill work, helping athletes build their fundamentals and confidence on the court. She also serves as a Head Coach on Clackamas High School’s women's JV2 volleyball team.

With over ten years of accounting and administrative experience in higher education, Kat has worn many hats within club volleyball, including administrative operations, registrations, communications, organizational logistics, and event coordination. Her experience both on the court and behind the scenes support the athletes, coaches, and families of HVVC.

name: Eden Erickson
bio:
Eden discovered her passion for volleyball at age 12 when she first joined the AGAPE Volleyball Club. She later joined North Clackamas Volleyball Club and played for Clackamas High School until the pandemic ended her season. Eden brings her lifelong love of the game to every practice, helping young athletes refine their technique, embrace the power of teamwork, and unlock their full potential.

Eden partners with her husband, Tatum, whose expertise in training and strength-and-conditioning complements her coaching. Together, they focus on building both skill and strength in HVVC's athletes. Outside of coaching, Eden is pursuing a career in radiology as an X-ray technician.
